sections.h2: How do you get a deed recorded in Allegan County?
sections.html:
You can record electronically or on paper at the Allegan County Register of Deeds. The county's register page names three e-recording vendors: CSC at 866-652-0111, Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and ePN, the E-Recording Partners Network, at 888-325-3365.

Most title companies already use one of those platforms, so a seller rarely deals with them directly. The page also links a land records search portal, the state's recording requirements, and the county's annual clerk and register reports.

The register records deeds, land contracts, mortgages, liens and leases, then stamps the document with the book, called a liber, where it is entered. A copy or image is kept as the permanent record, since the office does not keep the original deed or mortgage. The office says it does not prepare documents or answer legal questions, so it points people to an attorney or title company.

sections.h2: What does Allegan County charge to record and copy documents?
sections.html:
The recording fee is $30 per document no matter the page count, and the rule sits in MCL 600.2567. The rest of the schedule in that section is short.

  • $3 per extra instrument when a single paper assigns or discharges more than one.
  • $1 a page for copies and $5 to certify a recorded document.
  • 50 cents per year searched for grantor and grantee, minimum $5.
  • $1 to file or search for any other paper.

Payment is due when the document is left for recording. An electronic filing gets a little more room, because an e-recorded document's fee may be paid electronically within one business day of receipt.

The statute counts a "page" as one side of a sheet at least 8 1/2 by 11 inches and no longer than 14, in 20 pound paper or heavier. That definition matters only for copy charges.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will you owe in Allegan County?
sections.html:
Allegan County's median owner-occupied home value is $267,100 in the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures, well above the $162,800 for Alcona County and $153,900 for Alpena County. State and county transfer tax together run $4.30 per $500 of value, with each partial $500 rounded up.

Transfer tax at three sale prices in Allegan County, using $0.55 per $500 (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 per $500 (MCL 207.525)

The seller is the liable party under MCL 207.523, though a buyer may pay it on the seller's behalf. The county treasurer collects it, due 15 days after delivery of the instrument.

sections.h2: Which Allegan County transfers can skip the tax?
sections.html:
MCL 207.526 exempts a list of transfers, and a few come up often with houses in a lake or farm county like this one.

  • A deed that only straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A quitclaim deed given to confirm a title the grantee already holds, such as one that corrects a flaw.
  • A transfer between a limited liability company and its members when ownership shares are unchanged.
  • A transfer between a partnership and its partners on the same terms.
  • A deed in which the grantor is a government body or officer acting officially.

Anyone relying on one of these should say so to the title agent before closing. A refund request goes to the Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: What does the Allegan County Treasurer handle in a sale?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's Office certifies deeds, keeps tax histories, and collects delinquent real estate tax for the 35 townships, cities and villages in the county. The county chose to run the whole tax reversion process in-house, including title searches, court hearings, foreclosure and sale.

A seller with delinquent tax should talk to the treasurer's staff first, because the office advances delinquent amounts to the local units through its revolving fund. The page links to pay delinquent taxes, search tax records and foreclosure sales.

The treasurer also describes how former owners can claim leftover foreclosure proceeds. For foreclosures starting in 2021, a person with title or equity must file Form 5743 with the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 after the auctions with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow between February 1 and May 15. These steps come from MCL 211.78t.

sections.h2: Who sets and bills property tax in Allegan County?
sections.html:
Assessing happens at the township or city level, with the county Equalization Department publishing property records, a township and city assessor list, equalization reports and a tax levies and millages page. The county treasurer's page describes accounting for tax collections of the 35 local units and collecting delinquent real estate tax.

Because 24 townships, 9 cities and 2 villages each act as their own unit, the correct office depends on the parcel. The county's directory lists addresses and phone lines for all of them, such as Allegan Township at 269-673-5051, Otsego City Hall at 269-692-3391 and Holland City Hall at 616-355-1300.

Ask your township or city for the current tax balance before you list the house.

sections.h2: What is Allegan County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Allegan County was laid out in 1831 and organized in 1835. The county seat is the city of Allegan, and Holland is the largest city. It covers 825 square miles of land and counts as the Holland micropolitan area, part of the Grand Rapids combined area. The area is mostly agricultural and is urbanizing as Grand Rapids and Kalamazoo spread toward it.

The Lake Michigan shore draws vacation homes, especially around Saugatuck and Douglas. The Allegan State Game Area covers about 45,000 acres, Saugatuck Dunes State Park has dune trails and a swim beach, and Lake Allegan is another destination. A Pottawatomi band, the Match-e-be-nash-she-wish Band, has a reservation in the county.

The 2025 Census estimate is 123,188 residents, up 2.2 percent from April 2020. Owners live in 87.4 percent of homes, median household income is $83,283, and the mean commute is 24.2 minutes. The county issued 399 building permits in 2025.

faqs.q: Which e-recording services does Allegan County accept?
faqs.a: Allegan County accepts e-recording through CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Their numbers are 866-652-0111, 800-460-5657 and 888-325-3365.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Allegan County?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, plus $3 for each additional instrument assigned or discharged. Copies are $1 a page and certifying a recorded document costs $5.

faqs.q: How much is the state transfer tax on a $267,100 house in Allegan County?
faqs.a: It is $2,006.25 for the state, since $267,100 holds 535 units of $500 at $3.75 each. The county adds $294.25, which brings the total to $2,300.50.

faqs.q: Does the Allegan County register give legal advice or prepare deeds?
faqs.a: No. The office states it neither prepares documents nor answers legal questions, so use an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: Where do I file a claim for leftover foreclosure money in Allegan County?
faqs.a: File Form 5743 with the Allegan County Treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county answers by January 31 with Form 5744, and a circuit court motion can follow.
